aspects.says: A chip's cryptogram is a MAC over the amount, currency, date, type, the terminal's random number and the counter; the issuer recomputes it, so a hop that changes a covered value makes the card look counterfeit, and DE 55 passes through unchanged.
basis: section:14.1. A Chip Purchase Carries a Cryptogram Over Its Own Data, So Nobody on the Path May Change That Data

aspects.says: A merchant app that may detokenize puts every card number back in reach of a breach of that app, whatever the tokens look like.
basis: section:14.5. Only the Component That Builds the Network Message May Turn a Token Back Into a Card Number

aspects.says: Only the station that builds the network message may detokenize, for the token's own requestor; unknown, revoked or foreign tokens are refused before anything reaches the issuer, and a revoked card gets a new token.
basis: section:14.5. Only the Component That Builds the Network Message May Turn a Token Back Into a Card Number

aspects.says: The 3-D Secure result (ECI, authentication value, DS transaction ID) must travel in the authorization; a hop that drops it turns an authenticated purchase into an unauthenticated one, declined where authentication is required and a fraud chargeback for the merchant elsewhere.
basis: section:14.2. A 3-D Secure Result Rides in the Authorization, and a Hop That Drops It Drops the Proof

aspects.says: A token is issued per requestor and found through the keyed lookup value, never the card number, so a token leaked from one merchant is useless at another.
basis: section:14.4. A Token Belongs to the Requestor It Was Issued To

aspects.says: A token's digits are random, not derived from the card; it has sixteen digits and a correct check digit so card-number systems accept it, and a reserved BIN so it can never be a real card; a draw already taken is drawn again.
basis: section:14.3. A Token Is Random, Shaped Like a Card Number Under a BIN of Its Own

aspects.says: A random token outside a reserved range can be a real card number, so a token that escapes into a system that doesn't know it charges a stranger's card.
basis: section:14.3. A Token Is Random, Shaped Like a Card Number Under a BIN of Its Own
